references.text: Aaron asks Moses for forgiveness and intercedes, just as he did after the incident with the golden calf, where he acknowledged the people's sin.
Pharaoh uses similar language when he asks Moses for forgiveness and admits his sin.
King Saul uses the same expression 'I have acted foolishly' (נוֹאַלְתִּי) when he admits his sin to David.
The expression 'בִּי אֲדֹנִי' (oh, my lord) is used as a humble plea for mercy, just as Judah spoke to Joseph.
Moses responds to Aaron's prayer by crying out to God for Miriam's healing, showing that he accepted their repentance.
A similar prayer asking God not to count sin against the sinner, who pleads for mercy and forgiveness.
David uses the same expression about having acted foolishly (נוֹאַלְתִּי) when he admits his sin regarding the census.
